title: Trump's state capitalism reaches a high-water mark
gist: PIIE argues Trump's second-term state capitalism, about $24.5 billion of federal equity-linked stakes (June 2025-August 2026) concentrated in chips, critical minerals and quantum, plus forced foreign FDI pledges headlined at $5 trillion but realistically under $300 billion a year, is a historic high-water mark yet small against $765 billion of 2026 US AI investment. It expects the policy to peak with Trump and to do little to narrow China's lead.

insights.claim: The US government has committed about $24.5 billion in equity-linked support (loans, grants, warrants, price floors, offtakes, equity) across roughly three dozen deals between June 2025 and August 2026, concentrated in semiconductors, critical minerals and quantum computing.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Federal equity-linked backing is now a repeatable financing channel; small caps in these three sectors carry a non-trivial policy-put/dilution-risk profile.

insights.claim: Intel is by far the largest single federal stake at $8.9 billion (August 2025, warrants and equity), followed by Lithium Americas at $2 billion and Crucible Metals (Korea Zinc JV) at $1.6 billion.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Intel's stake dwarfs the rest, so the government is a major aligned stakeholder in the US foundry outcome.
insights.locator: Federal equity and ownership stakes table

insights.claim: The May 21, 2026 batch put roughly $100 million equity each into Atom Computing, D-Wave, Infleqtion, PsiQuantum, Quantinuum and Rigetti, plus $1 billion into IBM's Anderon quantum foundry, signalling a state-backed quantum buildout.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Quantum names now have a federal equity backstop; expect the sector to trade partly on Washington announcements.
insights.locator: Federal equity and ownership stakes table

insights.claim: A wave of July 29, 2026 deals took equity in small semiconductor firms (Kepler Computing, Multibeam, Extropic, Thintronics, OBSIDIA, Aeluma), with 2026 deal flow accelerating toward ever-smaller tickets.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Ticket sizes of $30-250 million suggest a venture-style federal portfolio strategy, not just rescues of big names.
insights.locator: Federal equity and ownership stakes table

insights.claim: Trump's state capitalism differs from past bailouts: earlier rescues (Penn Central, Lockheed, Chrysler 1980) used loan guarantees and were short-term, whereas today's stakes are durable equity ownership outside emergencies.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Exit timelines are unclear; unlike 2008 stakes sold when the crisis receded, these may become permanent shareholders with veto or pricing influence.
insights.quote: These earlier bailouts entailed loan guarantees, not equity stakes, and were short-term rescue operations

insights.claim: Unlike tariffs, quotas and tax credits that benefit whole industries, state capitalism confers benefits on a single targeted firm, which increases the corruption and favoritism risk that historically made Republicans object.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Single-firm targeting makes winners political choices; idiosyncratic policy risk for names inside and outside the portfolio.
insights.quote: State capitalism, on the other hand, confers its benefits on a single targeted firm.
insights.locator: Trump's state capitalism reaches a high-water mark (intro)

insights.claim: Trump demanded a 'golden share' with veto rights from Nippon Steel as a condition for acquiring U.S. Steel in 2025, a template for government control with zero cash outlay.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Cross-border M&A into US strategic sectors may now come with governance concessions; price in a government veto.

insights.claim: Headline foreign investment pledges extracted by the administration total about $5 trillion, but annualized over stated horizons (10 years assumed where none given) they equal roughly $880 billion per year.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Treat the $5 trillion headline as marketing; the annualized figure is the one to compare against capex data.

insights.claim: Realistic forced FDI will likely not exceed $300 billion a year, since the pledges mix in imports and military purchases, are often nonbinding, and Gulf investment is doubtful after the Iran war; total US inward FDI in 2025 was only $232 billion.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Expect large shortfalls versus announced pledges; fade stocks priced on full delivery of Gulf money.
insights.quote: it seems improbable that forced FDI will double that figure

insights.claim: Japan pledged $550 billion (September 2025) and South Korea $350 billion (November 2025) in US projects, subject to US approval overseen by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, in exchange for a 15 percent cap on US tariffs.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: The tariff cap is the quid pro quo; project selection by Commerce makes allocation discretionary and politically steerable.

insights.claim: On September 30, 2026 the administration announced up to $200 billion of Korean power investment, including a Texas power facility and eight nuclear plants and an LNG facility in Alaska, timed to help struggling Republican Senate candidates in those states.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Announcement timing follows the electoral calendar; discount the odds of execution if political support fades after November.
insights.quote: The announcements were a classic example of the politicization of industrial policy

insights.claim: Of the Korean total, about $150 billion is committed to shipbuilding and $22 billion to a gas-fired power plant, while the Alaskan LNG plant remains in contention.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Shipbuilding is the most concrete component of Korean pledges; Alaska LNG remains unproven.

insights.claim: Gulf states' forced FDI promises may not outlive Trump's term, since they face Iran war recovery costs and may not follow through after he leaves the White House in 2029.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Pledges from Gulf sovereign investors carry a political-tenure discount.

insights.claim: Even combining federal equity outlays and forced foreign FDI, state-capitalist investment might reach at most about $330 billion a year, small against Goldman Sachs' forecast of $765 billion of US AI investment in 2026 and $4.85 trillion of total business fixed investment.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Private AI capex, not state capitalism, drives US investment; state stakes matter for niches but are not a macro driver.
insights.quote: State capitalism funded by the federal government, together with ventures financed by foreign countries, might at most amount to $330 billion annually.
insights.locator: While large-scale state capitalism is relatively new

insights.claim: The authors argue it would be wrong to see Trump's initiatives as a major transformation of the US economy.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Position for sector-specific winners, not a regime shift in the economy.
insights.quote: it would be wrong to attribute Trump's initiatives with a major transformation of the US economy
insights.locator: While large-scale state capitalism is relatively new

insights.claim: US fiscal deficits and debt leave little capacity to escalate state capitalism, while Social Security trust funds depleting at the end of 2032 and replenishing military equipment after the Iran war compete for resources.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: A fiscal ceiling caps the number of future stakes; rising entitlements and defense restocking crowd out industrial equity.
insights.quote: Given the size of US fiscal deficits and federal debt
insights.locator: Given the size of US fiscal deficits

insights.claim: Per a Stanford analysis cited, China has over 362,000 wholly state-owned enterprises, plus many partially owned, collectively controlling about two-thirds of industrial assets, orders of magnitude beyond US efforts.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: The US cannot match Chinese state ownership by scale; the stakes are a signal more than a competitive answer.

insights.claim: US state capitalism is unlikely to meaningfully narrow China's lead over the next decade, and crediting China's state capitalism for its tech achievements is itself doubtful.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Fade the narrative that equity stakes will close the US-China industrial gap.
insights.quote: it would be a major error to imagine that the recent US embrace will meaningfully narrow China's lead

insights.claim: More than half of China's top 100 companies are private or mixed ownership and tend to be the most dynamic, per Tianlei Huang and Nicolas Veron, undermining the case that state ownership drives performance.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Dynamic Chinese leaders are not purely state-owned, so copying China's state ownership may copy the wrong feature.
insights.locator: On the other hand, as Tianlei Huang

insights.claim: Advanced economies are all resurrecting equity deals: the US, UK, Canada, Australia and EU announced 69 equity deals in the first seven months of 2026, versus 51 in the same window of 2025 and 12 in 2023, with the US at 21.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: State equity is a multi-country trend growing about fivefold in three years, not just a Trump quirk.
insights.locator: Trump was not alone among advanced economies

insights.claim: Trump's second term will be a high-water mark for US state capitalism, unlikely to be exceeded after he leaves office whether Democrats sweep in 2026 and 2028 or Republicans retain control.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Expect existing stakes to be managed or wound down rather than expanded; peak policy-driven support for these names may be near.
insights.quote: Trump's second term will represent a high-water mark for US state capitalism that is unlikely to be exceeded once Trump leaves office.

insights.claim: State capitalism by the US was historically opposed on grounds of anti-socialism ideology and fear that politicians playing favorites breed corruption, and the Trump revolution removed this Republican resistance, driven by alarm at Chinese industrial competition.
insights.speaker: Gary Clyde Hufbauer,Katelyn Hetrick
insights.so_what: Chinese competition has produced bipartisan acceptance of tools once taboo, so a future Democratic administration is unlikely to unwind them.
insights.locator: Objections to these and other episodes
